blocks.text: Sort (value, originalIndex) records so equal values are contiguous while every occurrence retains its output slot. For a nonempty input, initialize rank = 1 for the first sorted value and write it to output[originalIndex]. For each later record, increment rank only when its value differs from the previous sorted value, then write the current rank to output[originalIndex]. Thus duplicates share one rank, consecutive distinct values receive consecutive ranks, and the final array is source-aligned. An empty input produces an empty output without initializing a rank. Using sorted position as rank breaks both dense ties and source alignment.
